speaker_role: several admissions officers, apparently at Brown (one refers to 'a Brown sort of way'); names not given
key_insights: Officers read essays for writing ability, college readiness, and signs of resilience, love of learning and curiosity.
The essay is one of the few parts of the application entirely under the applicant's control.
Simple, everyday topics often work best; students wrongly think it must cover their whole life or be publishable.
Test of specificity: if the name were removed and the essay found by classmates, they should know whose it is.
Have someone who knows you read it and tell you what impression they took away.
A favorite example was a fast-food drive-through worker who framed himself as an observer of how people treat each other.
notable_or_distinctive: Concrete example of a favored essay (drive-through 'undercover anthropologist') and the dropped-essay voice test.
reliability_notes: Old (12y) compilation of short soundbites; institution inferred from one remark; generic overall.
